text: list class "htest" containing following components: statistic value normalized test statistic. parameter, n sample size, removal missing values. p.value p-value test. alternative character string describing alternative hypothesis. method character string indicating test performed. data.name character string giving name data. rvn value RVN statistic (shown screen). nm value NM statistic, numerator RVN (shown screen). mu mean value RVN statistic (shown screen). var variance RVN statistic (shown screen).

title: Bartels Rank Test of Randomness for Detecting Non-Random Order in Continuous Sequences — bartelsRankTest
text: Data must least measured ordinal scale. RVN test statistic $$RVN=\frac{\sum_{=1}^{n-1}(R_i-R_{+1})^2}{\sum_{=1}^{n}\left(R_i-(n+1)/2\right)^2}$$ \(R_i=rank(X_i), =1,\dots, n\). known \((RVN-2)/\sigma\) asymptotically standard normal, \(\sigma^2=\frac{4(n-2)(5n^2-2n-9)}{5n(n+1)(n-1)^2}\). using alternative "trend" null hypothesis randomness tested trend. using alternative "oscillation" null hypothesis randomness tested systematic oscillation. Missing values silently removed. Bartels test rank version von Neumann's test, see vonNeumannTest.

title: Barnard's Unconditional Test for Comparing Two Independent Proportions in a 2×2 Table — barnardTest
text: two fundamentally different exact tests comparing equality two binomial probabilities - Fisher's exact test (Fisher, 1925), Barnard's exact test (Barnard, 1945). Fisher's exact test (Fisher, 1925) popular two. fact, Fisher bitterly critical Barnard's proposal esoteric reasons go . 2 x 2 tables, Barnard's test powerful Fisher's, Barnard noted 1945 paper, much Fisher's chagrin. Anyway, perhaps due computational difficulty Barnard's widely used. (Mehta Senchaudhuri, 2003) Unconditional exact tests can performed binomial multinomial models. binomial model assumes row column margins () known advance, multinomial model assumes total sample size known beforehand.  binomial model, user needs specify margin fixed (default rows). Conditional tests (e.g., Fisher's exact test) row column margins fixed, uncommon design. (See Calhoun (2019) details.) x matrix, taken two-dimensional contingency table, hence entries nonnegative integers.  Otherwise, x y must vectors length. Incomplete cases removed, vectors coerced factor objects, contingency table computed . 2x2 contingency table, \(X=[n_1,n_2;n_3,n_4]\), normalized difference proportions two categories, given column, can written pooled variance (Score statistic) $$T(X)=\frac{\hat{p}_2-\hat{p}_1}{\sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})(\frac{1}{c_1}+\frac{1}{c_2})}},$$ \(\hat{p}=(n_1+n_3)/(n_1+n_2+n_3+n_4)\), \(\hat{p}_2=n_2/(n_2+n_4)\), \(\hat{p}_1=n_1/(n_1+n_3)\), \(c_1=n_1+n_3\) \(c_2=n_2+n_4\). Alternatively, unpooled variance (Wald statistic), difference proportions can written $$T(X)=\frac{\hat{p}_2-\hat{p}_1}{\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1(1-\hat{p}_1)}{c_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2(1-\hat{p}_2)}{c_2}}}.$$ probability observing \(X\) $$P(X)=\frac{c_1!c_2!}{n_1!n_2!n_3!n_4!}p^{n_1+n_2}(1-p)^{n_3+n_4},$$ \(p\) unknown nuisance parameter. Barnard's test considers tables category sizes \(c_1\) \(c_2\) given \(p\). p-value sum probabilities tables score rejection region, e.g. significantly large difference proportions two-sided test. p-value test maximum p-value calculated \(p\) 0 1. useStoredCSM set TRUE companion data package called ExactData must installed GitHub. author states: "CSM test computationally intensive due iteratively maximizing p-value calculation order tables. CSM ordering matrix stored possible sample sizes less equal 100 (.e., max(n1,n2)<=100). Thus, using useStoredCSM = TRUE can greatly improve computation time. However, stored ordering matrix computed npNumbers=100 possible ordering matrix optimal larger npNumbers. Increasing npNumbers setting useStoredCSM = FALSE ensures p-value correctly calculated expense significantly greater computation time. stored ordering matrix used calculation confidence intervals non-inferiority tests, CSM can still computationally intensive."

title: Confidence Intervals for Binomial Proportions — binomCI
text: arguments vectorized recycled according standard R rules. Wald: Obtained inverting acceptance region large-sample normal (Wald) test. Wald continuity correction: continuity-corrected version Wald interval, obtained adding 1/(2n) standard Wald limits. Wilson (default): Introduced Wilson (1927), interval obtained inverting central limit theorem approximation family equal-tail tests \(p = p_0\). recommended Agresti Coull (1998) Brown et al. (2001). interval returned conf.int prop.test correct = FALSE. Wilson continuity correction: continuity-corrected modification Wilson interval. corresponds prop.test correct = TRUE. Modified Wilson: adjustment Wilson interval extreme counts (.e., \(x\) close 0 \(n\)), proposed Brown et al. (2001). Agresti-Coull: simplified modification Wilson interval (Agresti Coull, 1998). intervals never shorter Wilson intervals (Brown et al., 2001). internally used adjusted estimator \(\tilde{p}\) returned attribute. Jeffreys: equal-tailed Bayesian interval based Jeffreys prior, described Brown et al. (2001). Modified Jeffreys: modification Jeffreys interval boundary cases (e.g., \(x = 0\), \(x = n\), near-boundary values), following Brown et al. (2001). Clopper-Pearson: -called exact interval, based quantiles corresponding beta distribution. Arcsine: Based variance-stabilizing arcsine transformation binomial distribution. Logit: Obtained constructing Wald-type interval log-odds scale transforming back probability scale. Witting: randomized procedure (Witting, 1985) providing uniformly optimal lower upper confidence bounds binomial proportions. Repeated calls may yield slightly different results unless random number generator seed fixed. Pratt: Based highly accurate normal approximation (Pratt, 1968). Mid-p: Designed reduce conservatism Clopper-Pearson interval. lower bound \(p_l\) solves $$\frac{1}{2} f(x; n, p_l) + (1 - F(x; n, p_l)) = \frac{\alpha}{2}$$ upper bound \(p_u\) solves $$\frac{1}{2} f(x; n, p_u) + F(x - 1; n, p_u) = \frac{\alpha}{2}$$ \(f\) \(F\) denote binomial probability mass cumulative distribution functions. \(x = 0\) lower bound set 0; \(x = n\) upper bound set 1. Likelihood-based: Confidence intervals obtained profiling binomial deviance neighbourhood maximum likelihood estimator. Blaker: exact interval based method proposed Blaker (2000). Khouadji: transformation-based approximation binomial confidence intervals. applies variance-stabilizing transformation sample proportion, constructs normal-based interval, back-transforms original scale. Compared Wald interval stable small samples, rarely used practice compared methods like Wilson exact intervals. methods may produce limits outside admissible range \([0, 1]\). cases, bounds truncated remain within valid parameter space. methods "wilson", "wilson-cc", "wilson-mod", "agresti-coull", "witting", "arcsine", internally used adjusted point estimator can returned setting stdEst = FALSE. estimators typically slightly shrunk toward 0.5 compared usual estimator \(x/n\). See cited literature details. Required Samplesize (binomCIn()):  required sample size given confidence interval width depends assumed population proportion. Since proportion often unknown planning stage study, conservative approach use worst-case scenario \(p = 0.5\), maximizes variance therefore yields largest required sample size. accurate estimate population proportion available, can used obtain smaller required sample size level precision.

Agresti-Caffo: simple adjustment Wald interval (Agresti Caffo, 2000) obtained adding one success one failure group. approach performs well many practical situations. Newcombe score: Based inverting Wilson score interval proportion combining obtain interval difference (Newcombe, 1998). Newcombe score continuity correction: continuity-corrected variant Newcombe score method. Miettinen-Nurminen: Based restricted maximum likelihood estimation obtained solving cubic equation (Miettinen Nurminen, 1985). Often recommended small moderate sample sizes. Brown-Li-Jeffreys: method proposed Brown Li (2005). Hauck-Anderson: large-sample method described Hauck Anderson (1986). Beal: asymptotic method intended use small samples (Beal, 1987). Haldane: Described Newcombe (1998), based adding 0.5 cells. Jeffreys-Perks: Also described Newcombe (1998), based Bayesian-type adjustments. methods may produce limits outside admissible parameter space \([-1, 1]\). cases, interval bounds truncated remain within valid range. interval used? choice method remains active topic discussion. Wald interval known perform poorly many practical situations. Reviews Fagerland et al. (2011) provide comparative evaluations recommendations. Miettinen-Nurminen might sensible default. Newcombe-Score almost equivalent.

(1978). method simple widely used may perform poorly small sample sizes proportions close 0 1. Adjusted-log: continuity-adjusted modification Katz interval using additive corrections reduce bias improve performance sparse data settings (Walter, 1975; Pettigrew et al., 1986). Bailey: skewness-corrected interval proposed Bailey (1987) based cubic transformation. Often provides improved coverage probabilities relative standard Wald-type intervals. Koopman: asymptotic score interval obtained inverting Pearson's chi-square statistic (Koopman, 1984). Confidence limits determined iteratively via root-finding method generally considered among reliable asymptotic procedures. Noether: large-sample interval based directly asymptotic variance estimated ratio (Noether, 1957). Inverse hyperbolic sine: Based variance-stabilizing inverse hyperbolic sine transformation proposed Newcombe (2001). Several methods require special handling cases \(x_1 = 0\), \(x_2 = 0\), \(x_1 = n_1\), \(x_2 = n_2\). Small continuity corrections therefore applied internally needed. methods may produce infinite limits one observed proportion zero. expected behavior ratio parameters. interval used? choice method remains active topic discussion. Koopman interval often recommended due comparatively good coverage properties across broad range scenarios.

text: dunnTest performs post hoc pairwise multiple-comparison procedure appropriate rejection Kruskal-Wallis null hypothesis. contrast performing separate Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, Dunn's procedure preserves pooled ranking variance estimate underlying Kruskal-Wallis test. intended post hoc procedure following significant Kruskal-Wallis test, .e. typically three groups. x list, elements taken samples compared must numeric vectors. case g ignored. title: Levene's Test for Comparing Variances Across Groups — leveneTest
text: Let \(X_{ij}\) jth observation X ith group. Let \(Z_{ij} = |X_{ij} - X_i|\), \(X_i\) center (default median) X ith group. Levene's test statistic $$W_0 = \frac{\sum_i n_i (\bar{Z}_i - \bar{Z})^2 / (g - 1)}{\sum_i \sum_j (Z_{ij} - \bar{Z}_i)^2 / \sum_i (n_i - 1)}$$ \(n_i\) number observations group g number groups. Using median instead mean \(X_i\) yields robust variant known Brown-Forsythe test, default .

text: Performs Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) test composite hypothesis normality, see e.g. Thode (2002, Sec. 5.1.1). Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) test EDF omnibus test composite hypothesis normality. test statistic maximal absolute difference empirical hypothetical cumulative distribution function. may computed \(D = \max\{D^{+}, D^{-}\}\) $$D^{+} = \max_{=1,\ldots,n}\{/n - p_{()}\}, \quad D^{-} = \max_{=1,\ldots,n}\{p_{()} - (-1)/n\},$$ \(p_{()} = \Phi([x_{()} - \bar{x}]/s)\). , \(\Phi\) cumulative distribution function standard normal distribution, \(\bar{x}\) \(s\) mean standard deviation data values. p-value computed Dallal-Wilkinson (1986) formula, claimed reliable p-value smaller 0.1. Dallal-Wilkinson p-value turns greater 0.1, p-value computed distribution modified statistic \(Z = D(\sqrt{n} - 0.01 + 0.85/\sqrt{n})\), see Stephens (1974), actual p-value formula obtained simulation approximation process. Missing values silently removed.

text: Tests linear trend two-way \(r \times c\) contingency table computing Mantel linear--linear association statistic $$Q_{MH} = (n - 1) \cdot r^2$$ \(r\) Pearson correlation row column variables using supplied scores. null hypothesis linear association, \(Q\) asymptotic chi-squared distribution one degree freedom. test sometimes called Mantel-Haenszel chi-squared test trend, stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test \(2 \times 2 \times k\) tables (see mantelhaen.test ). score test ordinal association, also known linear--linear association test. variables measured ordinal scale. x numeric row /column dimnames (e.g. income brackets dose levels stored label strings parse numbers), values used default scores; otherwise default 1:nrow(x) resp. 1:ncol(x), .e. categories assumed equally spaced. mirrors scoring convention used cochranArmitageTest. choice scores affects result: monotone scores permitted; non-monotone scores (neither strictly increasing strictly decreasing) produce warning, since \(r\) longer reflect consistent ordinal trend.

title: Moses Test of Extreme Reactions for Comparing Extreme-Value Behaviour Between Two Groups — mosesTest
text: nonparametric test comparing spread (range) two independent groups, assessing whether control group shows greater variability experiment group. Distributional derivation. null hypothesis, assignment \(n_k + n_e\) pooled ranks two groups equally likely. exact distribution span \(S\) control group (subset size \(n_k\) drawn without replacement \(\{1, \ldots, N\}\)) given Moses (1952) : $$P(S \le s) = \frac{1}{\binom{N}{n_k}}   \sum_{=0}^{\min(s - n_k,\, n_e)}   \binom{+ n_k - 2}{}\,   \binom{n_e + 1 - }{n_e - }$$ cumulative distribution function (CDF): \(P(\mathrm{span} \le s)\). one-tailed p-value observed span \(S_{obs}\) : $$ p = P(S \ge S_{obs})   = 1 - P(S \le S_{obs} - 1) $$ distinction matters textbook presentations write summation formula \(P(S = s)\), whereas upper-tail probability required hypothesis testing obtained cumulative form. Generalisation trimming (\(h > 0\)). removing \(h\) extreme ranks end sorted control group ranks, effective control-group size becomes \(n_k^\prime = n_k - 2h\), yielding: $$ P(S_h \le s) = \frac{1}{\binom{N}{n_k}} \sum_{=0}^{\min(s - n_k^\prime,\, n_e)} \binom{+ n_k^\prime - 2}{}\, \binom{n_e + 2h + 1 - }{n_e - } $$ Tie handling. exact combinatorial distribution assumes continuous underlying distribution (ties). default, ties.method = "first" passed rank, producing integer-valued ranks remain compatible exact formula. Tied observations ordered according occurrence pooled sample, matching SPSS behaviour. Alternative tie methods "average" may produce fractional mid-ranks. cases span rounded upward via ceiling() retain integer-valued test statistic, resulting p-values regarded approximate rather exact. Numerical stability. exact distribution evaluated entirely log-space using lchoose log-sum-exp transformation, avoiding overflow large sample sizes.

title: Post Hoc Tests for Multiple Comparisons Following Anova — postHoc
text: Post hoc tests differ strongly control type error. Conservative methods reduce false positives lower power, liberal methods increase power cost higher false positive rate. LSD (Fisher):    adjustment multiple testing; highest power inflated type error. Mainly suitable small number groups. Bonferroni (Dunn's (Bonferroni) t-test):    Adjusts p-values number comparisons; simple robust, often overly conservative. Tukey HSD:    Controls family-wise error rate pairwise comparisons; widely used generally recommended balanced designs. Newman-Keuls:    Stepwise procedure power Tukey, weaker error control; may inflate type error. Duncan:    Similar Newman-Keuls liberal; provides higher power cost increased false positives. Scheffé:    conservative; suitable pairwise complex (contrast-based) comparisons. Guidance Tukey HSD typically good default pairwise comparisons. Bonferroni useful strict error control required. Scheffé appropriate complex contrasts. Tables  tables pairwise chi-square tests can performed, either without correction correction multiple testing following logic p.adjust.

title: Runs Test for Detecting Non-Random Order in Sequences — runsTest
text: Performs test whether elements x serially independent counting many runs threshold. y supplied, two-sample Wald-Wolfowitz test equality two distributions computed. runs test randomness requires dichotomous sequence. numeric variable x two distinct values, sequence dichotomised comparing observation median. Observations exactly equal median removed test, standard runs test literature. use different threshold, pass logical vector directly: runsTest(x > mean(x)). normal approximation uses expected number runs null $$\mu_r = \frac{2 n_0 n_1}{n_0 + n_1} + 1$$ variance $$\sigma_r^2 = \frac{2 n_0 n_1 (2 n_0 n_1 - n_0 - n_1)}{   (n_0 + n_1)^2 (n_0 + n_1 - 1)}$$ \(\hat{z} = (r - \mu_r + c) / \sigma_r\), \(n_0, n_1\) number values /threshold \(r\) number runs. Setting correct = TRUE applies continuity correction SAS (SPSS \(n < 50\)) : \(c = 0.5\) \(r < \mu_r\) \(c = -0.5\) \(r > \mu_r\). exact p-value computed conditional distribution number runs given \(n_0\) \(n_1\), implemented C++. Interpretation alternatives: "less": fewer runs expected — indicates clustering positive serial correlation. "greater": runs expected — indicates alternation negative serial correlation. "two.sided": departure either direction. Wald-Wolfowitz test two-sample nonparametric test equality two continuous distributions general alternatives. Exact p-values valid presence inter-group ties; warning issued ties detected.

what: Siegel-Tukey Test for Comparing Dispersion Between Two Independent Groups — siegelTukeyTest
title: Siegel-Tukey Test for Comparing Dispersion Between Two Independent Groups — siegelTukeyTest
text: Siegel-Tukey test examines null hypothesis variability (scale) x y equal. Rejection indicates two groups differ spread. test distribution-free assume normality, assume equal medians null hypothesis equal scale. medians differ, test may detect difference rather difference scale; use adjustMedian = TRUE remove median differences testing. Ranks assigned combined sorted sample pattern 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, ... extremes inward, 2, 3, 6, 7, ... second-lowest upward. combined sample size odd, median observation dropped ranking (taken larger group group sizes differ). Ties receive average ranks. p-value computed exactly (via pwilcox) ties samples smaller 50 observations; otherwise normal approximation tie-corrected variance used. behaviour can overridden exact. Note: Siegel-Tukey test relatively low power compared alternatives ansari.test mood.test, may indicate significance due median differences rather scale differences adjustMedian = FALSE.

title: Steel Test for Nonparametric Comparisons With a Common Control — steelTest
text: Performs Steel's many--one rank test independent samples. procedure nonparametric analogue Dunnett's test controls family-wise error rate comparing multiple treatment groups common control. test statistic based pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum statistics comparing treatment group control group. Ties handled using asymptotic variance covariance corrections described Scholz (2023). Adjusted p-values obtained asymptotic multivariate normal distribution standardized statistics. x list, elements taken samples compared hence numeric data vectors. case, g ignored one can simply use steelTest(x). P-values obtained multivariate normal distribution corresponding joint asymptotic distribution standardized Steel statistics.

title: Von Neumann's Successive Difference Test for Detecting Serial Dependence in Continuous Sequences — vonNeumannTest
text: test based von Neumann ratio statistic. VN test statistic unbiased case $$VN=\frac{\sum_{=1}^{n-1}(x_i-x_{+1})^2 \cdot n}{\sum_{=1}^{n}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2 \cdot (n-1)}$$ known \((VN-\mu)/\sigma\) asymptotically standard normal, \(\mu = 2n/(n-1)\) \(\sigma^2 = 4 n^2 (n-2) / [(n+1)(n-1)^3]\). VN test statistic original (biased) case $$VN=\frac{\sum_{=1}^{n-1}(x_i-x_{+1})^2}{ \sum_{=1}^{n}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2}$$ test statistic \((VN-2)/\sigma\) asymptotically standard normal, \(\sigma^2 = 4(n-2) / [(n+1)(n-1)]\). Missing values silently removed.
